title: Four binders, one cold reader
intro:
*Five minutes. Commit before you look.*

Four practitioners finished AI 201 and handed their workflow binder to someone who has never seen it, with the same instruction: **read the index and the runbook, then run step one. No questions.**

**One of them got started.** The other three stalled, and none of the three is missing an artifact.

artifacts.label: Binder A
artifacts.body:
**Index:** "Weekly competitor-brief workflow. Saves ~4 hrs/wk. Owner: me. Spec, pack, runbook, verification plan, autonomy profile, boundary sheet and rhythm doc all in the project knowledge."

All seven artifacts present and thorough. The spec describes a weekly cadence. The rhythm doc (written four modules later, after the workflow moved to a monthly deep-dive plus a lightweight weekly skim) describes a monthly cadence with a separate weekly variant. The runbook covers the monthly version. The verification plan's sample tally is from the weekly version and hasn't been re-run.

*Cold reader's note:* "Started on the weekly one because the spec said weekly. Got to runbook step 3 and it referenced a source list the weekly version doesn't have."

artifacts.label: Binder B
artifacts.body:
**Index:** "Client-onboarding summary pipeline. ~90 min/client saved, ~12 clients/mo. Owner: R. Okonkwo. **Start here:** open the runbook, use pack v4 (linked), sample input in /samples/anon-client-a.docx. Good output looks like /samples/target-output.md. If the summary is longer than one page, the pack is wrong, not the model."

All seven artifacts, consistent with each other. Runbook step one names the exact document to open, the exact prompt, and one line on what wrong looks like. Sample material is provided and pre-cleaned. Terms that are internal ("the intake sheet," "a green file") carry a one-line gloss the first time they appear.

*Cold reader's note:* "Ran step one in about eight minutes. Stalled once, on whether 'green file' meant approved or complete: the gloss said approved, I'd assumed complete."

artifacts.label: Binder C
artifacts.body:
**Index:** "Weekly market-signal workflow. Saves substantial analyst time. Owner: the insights team. Everything is in the project."

All seven artifacts, mutually consistent, and unusually well written: the spec in particular is the clearest document in the set. The runbook's step one reads: *"Pull the standard source set and run the extraction prompt against it, checking output against the usual quality bar before moving to step two."*

*Cold reader's note:* "Couldn't start. Don't know what the standard source set is, where the extraction prompt lives, or what the usual quality bar is. Every one of those is probably obvious if you built it."

artifacts.label: Binder D
artifacts.body:
**No index.** Six artifacts in the project knowledge, all current, all consistent, all detailed. The runbook is excellent and self-contained: step one names the file, the prompt and the failure mode. The verification plan has a live sample tally. The boundary sheet is complete with dated agreement answers.

The autonomy profile is the missing seventh: the workflow runs propose-then-approve at step 3, which is recorded in the runbook as a checkpoint but nowhere as a decision.

*Cold reader's note:* "Ran step one fine. Then spent twenty minutes working out which document to read next and whether I was allowed to let step 3 run unattended. Eventually guessed."

reasoning:
**B is the only binder the cold reader could start from, and its index is doing almost all of the work.** *Start here* names the first document, the pack version, the sample input and what good output looks like, plus one line on the most likely failure. That last sentence is the tell of someone who has watched a person get this wrong: *if the summary is longer than one page, the pack is wrong, not the model.*

And note what B's reader still stalled on: **"green file"** meant approved, they assumed complete. **B is not perfect and that is the point**, the handoff test's third question is *what did the doc assume I knew*, and the tacit-knowledge tax is never zero. It is one gloss away from fixed, because the gap is a word rather than a structure.

**A fails the consistency pass, which is the one this module says matters more than any single artifact.** Nothing is missing. Everything is thorough. And the spec says weekly while the rhythm doc says monthly, because the workflow changed in module 7 and the spec never caught up. The reader trusted the spec (correctly, it is the document that describes the workflow) and walked into a version that no longer exists. **Seven artifacts written at seven different times will drift unless somebody reads them together once**, and A is what happens when nobody does.

**C is the trap for good writers.** It is the best-written binder on the page and the reader could not start at all. *The standard source set. The extraction prompt. The usual quality bar.* Every one of those is a definite article pointing at something only the builder can see — and the builder cannot feel it, because to them the referent is obvious. **Clarity is not the same as sufficiency**, and "everything is in the project" is the sentence a builder writes when they have stopped being able to imagine not knowing where things are. C also fails the owner line: *the insights team* is not a person who can be asked.

**D is the closest to right and shows exactly what the index is for.** Six current, consistent, detailed artifacts and a genuinely excellent runbook: the reader *ran step one fine*. Then lost twenty minutes to navigation, and **guessed about an autonomy decision**, which is the expensive part. The autonomy profile isn't paperwork: it records what may run unattended, and a successor who guesses at that is the failure mode module 5 exists to prevent. **The index is one page and it is the page a successor reads first and an executive reads only**, D proves it by omission.

The transferable test, and it is the module's whole standard: **hand it to someone who cannot ask you a question.** A gets a version that no longer exists. C cannot begin. D begins and then guesses about the thing that matters. B begins in eight minutes and comes back with one word to fix.
